items.title: Virgin Atlantic Just Axed This 11-Hour Nonstop Heathrow Route: See Map Now
items.summary: Virgin Atlantic is ending its route from London Heathrow to the ever-popular Mexican tourist destination of Cancun. Flights from the UK's busiest airport only began in late 2025. While the seasonal service was due to pause in mid-April 2027, flights will not return in winter 2027/2028. Two weeks ago, Virgin confirmed that it'll stop Manchester-Las Vegas service .
items.t: Virgin Atlantic Just Axed This 11-Hour Nonstop Heathrow Route: See Map Now

items.title: Days After A Nationwide Ground Stop, 6 In 10 Americans Say Fares Are Air Travel's Biggest Problem
items.summary: On November 13, telecoms upgrade work led to a ground stop in the US, delaying 8,500 aircraft and causing 8,000 canceled flights. Yet, in a poll taken from November 17 to 19 by YouGov, high ticket prices continued to be named the largest problem by participants. Extra and hidden fees also scored highly.
items.t: Days After A Nationwide Ground Stop, 6 In 10 Americans Say Fares Are Air Travel's Biggest Problem

items.title: Mayday At 33,000 Feet: Leaky Faucet Floods Frontier Airlines Airbus A321neo Cabin
items.summary: In early-mid-November, a Frontier Airlines Airbus A321neo flying from Denver International to Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County had to divert to Chicago O'Hare after a leaky faucet flooded the floor of the passenger cabin. The pilots declared 'mayday' to air traffic control while cruising at 33,000 feet over eastern Iowa, and subsequently landed safely at Chicago O'Hare.
items.t: Mayday At 33,000 Feet: Leaky Faucet Floods Frontier Airlines Airbus A321neo Cabin

items.title: Grounded Since 2004: Brazil Revives 57-Year-Old Boeing 737 As Tourist Attraction
items.summary: Brazilian authorities have decided to breathe new life into an ex-VASP Boeing 737-200 by relocating it from Viracopos International Airport (VCP) in Campinas, São Paulo, to the city of Pedreira, some 25 miles (40 km) away. The aircraft last flew in 2004, and has since stayed on the ground in Campinas as a fire training aid. Now, however, it is set to become a tourist attraction that keeps the history of aviation alive.
items.t: Grounded Since 2004: Brazil Revives 57-Year-Old Boeing 737 As Tourist Attraction

items.title: Korean Air turns to smartphones to screen pilots and cabin crew for sleep apnea
items.summary:
Korean Air has started using smartphones to check whether its pilots, cabin crew and other employees are sleeping well enough to do their jobs safely.

The airline announced on November 26, 2026, that its Aviation Health and Medical Center has been running digital sleep assessments since September, for employees considered at higher risk of sleep disorders. Korean Air claims to be the first in the aviation industry to use a smartphone-based sleep apnea screening device, approved by South Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), for crew healthcare.

The program was developed with sleep-tech company Asleep and enables employees to monitor their sleep at home, without a hospital visit or specialized equipment.

Two apps track breathing and sleep rhythms at home 

The program has two parts. For sleep apnea screening, Korean Air uses Apnotrack. Employees place a smartphone next to their bed, and the app analyzes their breathing sounds over seven nights. Medical staff then review the results and refer employees to specialized sleep clinics if they need further evaluation or treatment.

The second app, ChronoTrack, focuses on sleep rhythms. Over 14 days, it records when employees fall asleep and wake up, and how regular their sleep is, to assess insomnia and disruptions to the body clock.

The tools target a group whose schedules make good sleep hard to come by. Pilots and cabin crew deal with long-haul flights, night operations and frequent time zone changes, while maintenance personnel work in shifts. Sleep apnea is also hard to spot, because it occurs while a person…
items.t: Korean Air turns to smartphones to screen pilots and cabin crew for sleep apnea

items.title: IndiGo Cancels All Flights To 9 International Destinations: See Full List Now
items.summary: IndiGo is overwhelmingly India's largest airline. In 2026, OAG data shows that the carrier has approximately 55% of the total flights to, from, and within India. While not a like-for-like comparison, Air India has 13% of the huge market.
items.t: IndiGo Cancels All Flights To 9 International Destinations: See Full List Now

items.title: Airbus A350-1000ULR Sets Extraordinary Nonstop Flight Distance Record
items.summary: In this video, we'll examine how Airbus achieved this extraordinary record, how it finally surpassed Boeing's legendary 777-200LR Worldliner, and what this milestone means for the future of ultra-long-haul travel.
items.t: Airbus A350-1000ULR Sets Extraordinary Nonstop Flight Distance Record

items.title: Why A Delta Air Lines Comeback In Memphis Could Be Bigger Than It Looks
items.summary: Delta Air Lines is quietly reshaping its presence at Memphis International Airport (MEM), more than a decade after abandoning its former hub. Although the airline has discontinued some routes and temporarily suspended others, it has also introduced new nonstop connections, including daily flights to John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK). These developments suggest that Memphis could be becoming a more important part of Delta's network again.
items.t: Why A Delta Air Lines Comeback In Memphis Could Be Bigger Than It Looks

items.title: How The Big 3 US Legacy Carriers Compare On Reliability In 2026
items.summary: Reliability remains one of the most important considerations for passengers choosing between the three largest legacy airlines in the US. Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, and American Airlines operate extensive domestic and international networks, connecting millions of passengers every year.
items.t: How The Big 3 US Legacy Carriers Compare On Reliability In 2026

items.title: AirAsia Philippines cuts jobs, faces strike as AirAsia Group delays staff salaries
items.summary:
AirAsia Philippines is to cut jobs and scale back routes and flight frequencies, with high jet fuel prices and a weak peso driving up its operating costs. Local media has reported that about 90 captains and first officers have been told their employment will end on December 31, 2026.

“AirAsia Philippines has made the very difficult decision to reduce our workforce. Sustained pressure from elevated jet fuel prices and unfavorable exchange rates has significantly increased our operating costs,” President and General Manager Anna Victoria Lu said in a statement on November 26, 2026.

“In response, we had to carefully evaluate and optimize our routes and flight frequencies to keep operations sustainable, which have a significant effect on our manpower requirements,” Lu added. “These tough adjustments are being made to ensure the long-term stability of the airline, in the best interest of our passengers and our dearest Allstars.”

The airline did not say how many employees were affected or which routes and flights will be cut, although local media, citing the pilots’ union, has reported that about 90 pilots have received retrenchment notices.

Lu stressed that the company would support those who are leaving. “We deeply recognize the impact this has on our colleagues and their families, and we are committed to supporting them with care and transparency through this transition,” she said.

The Philippine Star reported that AirAsia Philippines has been one of the country’s hardest-hit carriers, closing some flights to save costs as jet fuel crossed USD 200 per barrel. Like other…
items.t: AirAsia Philippines cuts jobs, faces strike as AirAsia Group delays staff salaries

items.title: 5 McDonnell Douglas Engineering Decisions That Became Permanent Features Of Boeing Aircraft After The 1997 Merger
items.summary: In August 1997, Boeing acquired McDonnell Douglas in a $13.4 billion deal that created the largest aerospace company in the world. Most of the discussion about the merger in the years since has focused on how McDonnell Douglas' business culture influenced Boeing's approach to cost management, engineering investment, and risk tolerance, and not favorably. The two fatal 737 MAX crashes in 2018 and 2019 brought that critique into sharp focus, with analysts drawing a direct line between McDonnell Douglas' preference for derivative designs and the engineering compromises that produced the MCAS system.
items.t: 5 McDonnell Douglas Engineering Decisions That Became Permanent Features Of Boeing Aircraft After The 1997 Merger

items.title: Boeing to win lion’s share of Qantas widebody order over Airbus: Bloomberg
items.summary:
Boeing is set to win the lion’s share of a potential Qantas widebody order over European rival Airbus, according to Bloomberg.

On November 27, 2026, Bloomberg claimed that an order for 20 aircraft from the Australian flag carrier is set to include Boeing 787 Dreamliners and some Airbus A350s.

The information is said to have been sourced from people with knowledge of developments involving the order.

In a statement to Bloomberg, Qantas said: “We are still in discussion with the relevant aircraft manufacturers as part of our widebody fleet planning and no decisions have been made.”

Steve Worner / Shutterstock 

This is not the first time that speculation of a potential new Qantas widebody order has circulated this year.

In June 2026, Reuters spoke with industry sources who said Qantas was looking at an order for 20 aircraft with both the 787 and A350 under consideration.

Qantas A380 retirement and upcoming A350-1000ULRs 

Qantas announced in August 2026 that its fleet of Airbus A380s would retire four years earlier than originally planned. They were expected to fly until at least until 2032, but this has now been brought forward to 2028.

With the A380 retirement in mind, Qantas will want to ensure it has additional long-haul aircraft capacity for the years ahead.

In April 2027, the first of 12 Airbus A350-1000ULR aircraft is due to join the airline, once all final tests have been completed.

The aircraft has just 238 seats – according to Qantas, the “lowest seat density of any A350 around the world” – and is designed to give travelers more space.

The A350-1000ULRs…
items.t: Boeing to win lion’s share of Qantas widebody order over Airbus: Bloomberg

items.title: Rolls-Royce Has Tripled The Time Between Boeing 787 Engine Overhauls With 1 Blade Redesign
items.summary: When designing an aircraft that promised to be as impactful as the 787 Dreamliner, Boeing required the most state-of-the-art engines that suppliers could deliver and then some. GE offered the GEnx-1B, but the Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 became closely associated with the program.
items.t: Rolls-Royce Has Tripled The Time Between Boeing 787 Engine Overhauls With 1 Blade Redesign

items.title: LATAM Airlines completes first E195 E2 flight, adds regional destinations
items.summary:
An expansion of LATAM Airlines’ regional route network in Brazil was announced by the company on November 26, 2026. 

The new services will link LATAM’s hub at São Paulo Guarulhos (GRU) and the country’s capital, Brasília (BSB), to six secondary cities across the country: Alta Floresta (AFL), Sorriso (SMT), Carajás (CKS), Altamira (ATM), Araguaína (AUX) and Ipatinga (IPN). 

Initially at least, the new services will run from June to October 2027. 

The airline timed this announcement to coincide with the first flight of a LATAM Embraer E195 E2 jet. The aircraft, which was delivered on October 8, 2026 , operated a special flight from São Paulo Guarulhos International Airport to Brasília Air Base. It was carrying 70 students from different schools and technical institutes, together with Embraer and LATAM executives and staff, who were welcomed by representatives of Brazil’s federal government. 

The trip was intended to highlight the importance of LATAM’s commitment to the operating E2 jets for the Brazilian manufacturer and the broader aerospace industry in the country. It also included a program of technical and cultural visits in the Brazilian capital. 

In September 2025, LATAM ordered 24 Embraer E2 jets , plus 50 additional options, with the specific idea of supporting better regional connectivity across Brazil. 

Earlier in 2026, LATAM’s CEO, Roberto Alvo, explained in an AeroTime Executive Spotlight interview that regional traffic is one of the areas of growth in which the carrier will be investing. This segment of the market still has a propensity to travel which is…
items.t: LATAM Airlines completes first E195 E2 flight, adds regional destinations

items.title: Leonardo rolls out first M-346 for Italy’s Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team
items.summary:
Leonardo has officially unveiled the first of 15 M-346 aircraft developed for the Italian Air Force’s Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team, as announced by the company on November 26, 2026. 

The aircraft was presented during a ceremony at Leonardo’s production facility in Venegono Superiore, in the province of Varese, where it also performed a flight demonstration. The jet had already made its maiden flight on October 29, 2026. 

Designated M-346 PAN after the team’s formal name, Pattuglia Acrobatica Nazionale (National Aerobatic Team), the twin-engine jet will replace the single-engine Aermacchi MB-339PAN flown by the Frecce Tricolori since 1982. 

Production and deliveries are scheduled for 2027 and 2028. In addition to the 15 aircraft, the program includes technical and logistical support, training and simulation systems for pilots and maintenance personnel, and infrastructure upgrades at Rivolto Air Base, near Udine, home to the 313th Aerobatic Training Squadron. 

Ci sono emozioni che attraversano le generazioni, storie che diventano parte dell’identità di un Paese e simboli che ne raccontano l’eccellenza.

Con l’M-346 PAN di #Leonardo e la nuova livrea firmata da Pininfarina, le Frecce Tricolori dell’Aeronautica Militare (@ItalianAirForce) raccolgono l’eredità dello storico MB-339 per scrivere una nuova pagina della loro straordinaria storia.

L’eccellenza tecnologica dell’industria aeronautica italiana incontra professionalità, disciplina, passione e dedizione dei piloti e degli specialisti dell’#AeronauticaMilitare. 

Nuove evoluzioni, nuove emozioni, ma lo stesso…
items.t: Leonardo rolls out first M-346 for Italy’s Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team

items.title: Russia extends ban on jet fuel exports as Ukrainian drones strain production
items.summary:
Russia is to ban jet fuel exports for an additional three months, with a previous deadline, set in June 2026, set to expire in the coming days.

On November 27, 2026, as speculation about an extension mounted, the Russian cabinet’s press service confirmed that a new temporary ban on exports of jet fuel would be imposed.

The resolution, signed by Russian officials, will ban all jet fuel exports, including fuel purchased in exchange trading, from December 1, 2026, until March 31, 2027. The current ban is set to expire on November 30, 2026.

The Russian cabinet asserted that the “decision was made to support a stable situation on the domestic fuel market”.

14th Separate Regiment of Unmanned Aerial Systems 

“The restrictions will not apply to, among other things, supplies of jet fuel under international intergovernmental agreements,” a spokesperson said. “The government is continuing work on maintaining reliable and uninterrupted fuel supplies for the domestic market.”

Russia’s main jet fuel customers are based in Central Asia, including countries such as Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries have strained jet fuel production, with the Kirishi Petroleum Organic Synthesis plant and the Slavneft-Yanos refinery among its targets.

According to APA , Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said recently that Russia’s fuel market remains “quite tense” due to the “fact that a number of refineries are under repair”. He added that deficits in fuel are being covered through external supplies.

Ukraine’s long-range attacks on…
items.t: Russia extends ban on jet fuel exports as Ukrainian drones strain production

items.title: Updated: Norse Atlantic suspends all operations as it runs out of cash
items.summary:
This story was first published on November 27, 2026, and updated the following day to reflect a new statement on the status of the airline’s leased fleet. 

Norse Atlantic Airways confirmed that it is suspending all operations due to its troubled financial situation. 

The announcement was made shortly before 9.00am local time on November 26, 2026, in an official statement sent to the Oslo Stock Exchange, where the airline is publicly listed. 

Rumors about an imminent grounding had already been swirling around for a number of hours, as the airline cancelled several of its flights overnight, including those operated for Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) under a wet-lease arrangement. 

The following day, Norse Atlantic Airways issued yet another statement informing that aircraft lessors had initiated the process to terminate leases on the airline’s entire fleet of 12 Boeing B787-9 aircraft.

Norse Atlantic Airways races to secure emergency financing 

Norse Atlantic Airways had already warned two days earlier that its liquidity position was critical and that it was frantically seeking fresh sources of funds in order to meet its short-term financial commitments. 

According to the latest statement, the board of directors is still considering several options to secure additional financing in a last-ditch effort to save the business. These include a potential takeover by an external party (an option that has reportedly been in consideration already for several months) as well as negotiations with bondholders in relation to an outstanding US$52 million senior secured bond.…
items.t: Norse Atlantic suspends all operations as it runs out of cash

items.title: Boeing’s Dave Schulte on why Southeast Asia will need 5,000 new jets by 2045
items.summary:
Boeing said it expects Southeast Asia to need almost 5,000 new commercial airplanes over the next two decades. According to the planemaker’s 2026 Commercial Market Outlook (CMO), the region will take delivery of 4,985 new aircraft between 2026 and 2045, more than tripling its fleet from 1,475 aircraft to 5,215. Three quarters of those deliveries will add new capacity rather than replace older jets.

AeroTime met with Dave Schulte, Managing Director of Commercial Marketing for Asia Pacific at Boeing, in Kuala Lumpur during the 70th Assembly of Presidents of the Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA). 

In an exclusive interview, Schulte discussed what is driving demand in the region, how the B737-10 is reshaping the narrowbody market, and why a difficult 2026 has not changed Boeing’s long-term view. He also shared where Indonesia, Southeast Asia’s largest aviation market, fits in the company’s plans.

Three quarters of demand is for growth 

The latest forecast is higher than the Southeast Asia outlook Boeing presented at the Singapore Airshow in February 2026, which called for 4,885 new airplanes.

Asked what is behind the revised number, Schulte pointed to the nature of the market rather than the age of today’s fleets. “Southeast Asia is a high-growth market, and so it’s one of the fastest-growing markets in the world,” he said. Only about a quarter of new deliveries will replace older aircraft. The CMO puts that at 1,245 airplanes, with the remaining 3,740 going toward growth.

Schulte said that growth reaches well beyond airlines. “When airplanes come into the…
items.t: Boeing’s Dave Schulte on why Southeast Asia will need 5,000 new jets by 2045

items.title: Italian Rheinmetall technicians killed in Kuwaiti drone explosion
items.summary:
Italy’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has confirmed that two Italian nationals working for defense firm Rheinmetall were killed in Kuwait following a drone explosion.

On November 26, 2026, Italian authorities said the Rheinmetall Italia workers were “performing maintenance on the detection antennas of the Skyguard anti-aircraft defense system” when the drone strike occurred.

Earlier in the day, Colonel Saud Al-Atwan, a spokesperson for the Ministry of Defense, said that Kuwait Armed Forces had detected several hostile drones in the country’s air space and had engaged.

Colonel Al-Atwan blamed “heinous Iranian aggression” which targeted a “vital site”, causing shrapnel to fall on four people.

He described the four injured individuals as a Kuwaiti national, a Pakistani national and two Italians. All four were moved to the hospital for treatment.

Kuwait said the two Italian victims died from wounds sustained during the Iranian drone attack.

Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani is following the situation and expressed his condolences to the families of the deceased.

“The Italian Embassy in Kuwait is in constant contact with local authorities to monitor developments and provide the families of Italian nationals with the necessary information,” Italy’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said.

Colonel Al-Atwan added: “The Ministry extends its sincere condolences and sympathy to the families of the two deceased. Wishing a speedy recovery to the remaining injured.”

The post Italian…
items.t: Italian Rheinmetall technicians killed in Kuwaiti drone explosion

items.title: Positive Aviation commits €60M to convert ATR72 into amphibious water bomber
items.summary:
Positive Aviation, a French startup which is developing an amphibious retrofit of the ATR72 aircraft for firefighting missions, has announced an investment of €60 million to build two manufacturing facilities in France. 

The announcement was made shortly after Positive Aviation was confirmed as one projects selected for the 11th batch of the “Première Usine” program with the France 2030 initiative, a public program which selects industrial projects eligible to receive state funding on account of their strategic importance to France. 

In particular, Positive Aviation is planning to invest €36 million in its main industrial facility, which will be located in Toulouse, and will be dedicated to retrofitting ATR72 turboprops for their new role as firefighters. 

Another €24 million will be allocated to a new factory in Vannes, in northwestern France, to produce the floats affixed to the converted ATR72s, which will be called FF72s. 

Those floats, which will be produced in collaboration with Multiplast, a subsidiary of Groupe Carboman, are 18 meters long, and weigh 1.5 tons. They are also able to support landings on water at speeds of up to 185 km/h. 

However, this investment appears to be double what Positive Aviation has reportedly raised so far. According to multiple media sources, the French startup has raised approximately €30 million up to November 2026, with around half of that coming from private investors. Another €7 million has been provided by banks and €2.5 million by the Occitanie region of France, where Toulouse is located. The “Première Usine” program is…
items.t: Positive Aviation commits €60M to convert ATR72 into amphibious water bomber

items.title: airBaltic gets Latvian parliament backing for state guarantee
items.summary:
Latvia’s parliament has approved legislative amendments allowing the government to provide a state guarantee of up to €175 million ($192 million) to help airBaltic secure further private financing and avoid a potential grounding in December 2026.

The Saeima adopted the amendments to the airline’s financial stabilization measures law, originally passed on August 20, 2026, in their second and final reading on November 26, 2026, with 77 lawmakers voting in favor, 19 against and none abstaining. Earlier that day, lawmakers had approved the amendments in their first reading by 76 votes to 18, with no abstentions.

The legislation, fast-tracked through parliament, authorizes the Cabinet of Ministers to issue the guarantee. The money would come from private lenders, with the Latvian state guaranteeing the airline’s repayment obligations.

The vote follows the Latvian government’s approval in principle of the guarantee on November 24, 2026. The Saeima’s Budget and Finance (Taxation) Committee backed the proposal by nine votes to two a day later.

airBaltic risks grounding by mid-December 

airBaltic has been undergoing financial restructuring under Chapter 11 in the US since September 14, 2026.

On October 19, 2026, the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York gave final approval to up to €350 million ($383 million) in debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing. The package consists of three tranches: an initial €175 million ($192 million), followed by up to €125 million ($137 million) and up to €50 million ($55 million). The court had already granted interim access to…
items.t: airBaltic gets Latvian parliament’s backing for state guarantee

items.title: Russian Aerospace Forces weapons chief arrested pending bribery investigation
items.summary:
A military court in Moscow has ordered Colonel General Yuri Grekhov, the deputy commander-in-chief of the Russian Aerospace Forces (VKS) in charge of armaments, to be held in pretrial detention in a bribery case. 

The 235th Garrison Military Court granted a request from Russia’s military investigators on November 25, 2026, according to court records cited by multiple Russian news outlets on November 26, 2026. RBC reported that Grekhov had been remanded in custody for two months. 

Russian general faces up to 15 years in prison  

Citing two law enforcement sources, RBC reported that Grekhov is accused of accepting a bribe on an especially large scale under Part 6 of Article 290 of the Russian Criminal Code. The offense carries a prison sentence of eight to 15 years. 

Kommersant reported the same charge, citing sources close to the investigation. Neither publication disclosed the amount of the alleged bribe or what it was paid for. 

Grekhov denies the charge. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on November 26, 2026, that he had no information about the case, TASS reported . 

Who is Yuri Grekhov?  

Yuri Grekhov, deputy commander-in-chief of the Russian Aerospace Forces for armaments. (Credit: Kremlin) 

An air defense officer by training, Grekhov became chief of staff of Russia’s Air and Missile Defense Troops in 2013 before taking command of the force in 2018. The appointment also made him a deputy commander-in-chief of the Aerospace Forces. 

He took over responsibility for VKS armaments in 2021. As recently as 2025, Russian Ministry of Defense publications…
items.t: Russian Aerospace Forces weapons chief arrested pending bribery investigation

items.title: airBaltic offers staff Air Niugini secondment, demotion or departure: Reuters
items.summary:
airBaltic staff have been notified via email of several pathways open to them as the Baltic carrier looks to save costs and reduce the size of its workforce.

According to Reuters , airBaltic flight attendants have been presented with the choice between a demotion and termination of contract, while others have been given incentives to depart voluntarily.

airBaltic pilots have also been given a range of options including termination and a secondment with Air Niugini. Other pilots were also offered a demotion from the position of captain.

Reuters reported that it had seen emails sent to airBaltic staff and spoke to two people with knowledge of the process.

Airbus 

In a statement to Reuters airBaltic said the process is being conducted in “full compliance with applicable labor laws and regulations”.

“Different employee groups have been offered options such ‌as reduced ⁠workloads, alternative roles and transfers between bases, with the aim of minimizing the number of redundancies,” airBaltic said.

In response to developments the Latvian Aviation Union said it has “raised serious concerns, stating that it was not consulted on the demotions or secondment arrangements and questioning their compliance with Latvian and EU regulations”.

“Behind every restructuring decision are real people, their careers, families, livelihoods and professional futures,” the union wrote on LinkedIn. “Financial restructuring must not come at the expense of employees’ rights, fair treatment, transparency and meaningful social dialogue.”

airBaltic maintains efforts to drive down costs 

At the…
items.t: airBaltic offers staff Air Niugini secondment, demotion or departure: Reuters

items.title: Brazilian airline GOL to introduce new premium cabin across narrowbody fleet
items.summary:
Brazilian low-cost carrier GOL Linhas Aereas Inteligentes announced on November 25, 2026, that it will introduce a new premium product across its entire fleet from early 2027. 

The new offering, which will be called GOL Premium, will feature blocked middle seats, dedicated overhead bin compartments and crew attention, as well as priority boarding. The premium area of the cabin will comprise the first three rows of seats (12 seats in total per aircraft) and will be separated from the main cabin by a divider. 

Passengers on GOL Premium will also have access to a specific catering offering which will vary depending on the type of route. On international routes of up to three and a half hours and on domestic routes longer than two hours or those deemed to be “strategic” (basically trunk routes out of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro) meals will include a hot sandwich, chocolates, snacks and alcoholic or soft drinks. 

On shorter domestic routes, catering will be limited to sweet and savory snacks and drinks, while on international flights longer than three and half hours there is going to be a more complete meal option, with hot dishes, desserts, and a diversity of drinks. Amenity kits will also be distributed. 

GOL Premium will replace the existing “Gol+Conforto” product, which is essentially a regular economy class seat with extra leg room and recline. This new product will be available from February 15, 2027, on international and domestic flights, although it will be possible to book from December 15, 2026. 

The new premium product is part of the airline’s diversification…
items.t: Brazilian airline GOL to introduce new premium cabin across narrowbody fleet

items.title: US Navy orders three more E-130J Phoenix II nuclear communications aircraft
items.summary:
The US Navy has exercised a $1.13 billion contract option with Northrop Grumman for three more E-130J Phoenix II test aircraft, bringing the number of aircraft under contract for the development of its future airborne nuclear communications platform to six. 

According to the Pentagon’s contract announcement for November 25, 2026 , the award covers the design, development and delivery of three system demonstration test aircraft, as well as an initial supply of spare parts. Work is expected to be completed by January 2030. 

The US Navy has committed $4.18 million in fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation funds at the time of the award. Most of the work will take place in Melbourne, Florida (35%), Marietta, Georgia (23%), and Richardson, Texas (15%). 

US Navy doubles E-130J test fleet  

The E-130J is based on the stretched C-130J-30 Super Hercules, fitted with Take Charge and Move Out (TACAMO) mission equipment, including a very low frequency (VLF) communications system from Collins Aerospace. Northrop Grumman leads the program, with Collins Aerospace and Lockheed Martin as subcontractors. 

The US Navy’s initial $3.46 billion development contract , awarded in December 2024, covered three engineering development aircraft and included options for three additional test aircraft and up to six aircraft in an initial production batch. 

The latest award exercises the options for the three additional test aircraft. In March 2026, the US Navy also awarded Northrop Grumman a $225.1 million contract modification for the E-130J’s training systems. 

On October 15,…
items.t: US Navy orders three more E-130J Phoenix II nuclear communications aircraft

items.title: FedEx MD-11 overruns runway at Miami airport, triggering ground stop
items.summary:
A FedEx Express McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter overran a runway while landing at Miami International Airport (MIA) on the evening of November 25, 2026, forcing the closure of three of the airport’s four runways and triggering a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop on the eve of the US Thanksgiving holiday. 

The FAA identified the aircraft as FedEx Flight 910, which had departed Frederick W. Smith International Airport (MEM) in Memphis. Miami airport officials said the aircraft overran Runway 26R. Flight-tracking data identifies the jet as N605FE, an MD-11F manufactured in 1992, according to FAA registry records . 

The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office said two people were on board and that no injuries were reported. 

“We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries,” FedEx said in a statement, adding that it was coordinating with investigators. 

Runway overrun disrupts Thanksgiving travel  

Runway 8L/26R is the shortest of Miami International Airport’s four runways, measuring 2,621 meters (8,600 feet), according to airport data . Following the overrun, the airport temporarily closed all but one of its runways. 

The FAA issued a ground stop for Miami-bound flights before announcing in a social media post shortly after 21:30 local time that flights would soon resume. Disruptions continued into the early hours of November 26, 2026, with the FAA reporting delays of several hours. 

Second runway overrun at Miami airport in three months  

The incident comes less than three months after 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 freighter…
items.t: FedEx MD-11 overruns runway at Miami airport, triggering ground stop

items.title: Heathrow expansion in jeopardy as government fails to make case for third runway
items.summary:
A committee of British MPs have said the UK government has failed to make the case for a third runway at London-Heathrow Airport (LHR). 

On November 26, 2026, the Transport Committee delivered its verdict on the draft Heathrow Expansion National Policy Statement (HENPS) following five weeks of evidence gathering and examining the plans in detail. 

Attempts by the UK government to position expansion as “critical” to national growth also failed with the committee stating, “the case for this designation applying to Heathrow expansion has not been made”. 

The MP’s report criticized the “lack of an overall strategy for aviation and calls for more work to nail down the full range of benefits and costs”. 

Ung151 / Shutterstock.com 

“Plans for a third runway should be grounded for now and the government should go back to the drawing board before proceeding any further,” Transport Committee Chair Ruth Cadbury said. 

The Transport Committee has examined the views of organizations and stakeholders both supporting and opposing a third runway at Heathrow , including from the airport’s CEO Thomas Woldbye. 

MPs received 90 pieces of written evidence and questioned community groups, the aviation sector, academics, local authorities, economists, the Climate Change Committee, the promoters of both proposed third runway schemes, and the Minister for Aviation. 

The HENPS sets out that expansion will be assessed against a framework consisting of four tests, covering economic growth, climate, air quality, and noise.

items.title: Emirates and Etihad A380 aircraft among eight requiring EASA ordered inspections
items.summary:
Emirates and Etihad Airways Airbus A380 aircraft are among eight superjumbos that must undergo inspections after the European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) issued an Airworthiness Directive raising concerns around a “potential unsafe condition”.

The Airworthiness Directive (2026-0216) supersedes a previous instruction (2026-0119-E) issued in June 2026, requiring 16 Airbus A380s to receive wing mid spars inspections .

EASA previously said that this “condition, if not detected and corrected, could reduce the structural integrity of the wing”.

In the latest directive, which became effective on November 18, 2026, EASA explained that it was “determined that additional MSNs may be affected by the same potential unsafe condition”.

Andi_Munich / Creative Commons 

“Further analysis identified the need for updated inspection requirements,” EASA stated. Consequently, Airbus issued Alert Operators Transmission (AOT) A57R030-26.

The latest eight A380s must be inspected by January 31, 2027, in line with Airbus’ Alert Operators Transmission.

EASA also added that before A380s can return to service (RTS) after storage lasting more than 12 months, wing mid spars must be inspected in accordance with the instructions of the AOT.

“If, during any inspection any discrepancy is detected, before next flight, contact Airbus for applicable repair instructions and, within the compliance time specified in those instructions, accomplish those instructions accordingly,” EASA stated.

Which Airbus A380s are affected?

items.t: Emirates and Etihad A380 aircraft among eight requiring EASA ordered inspections

items.title: Ukrainian combat laser shoots down Russian jet-powered Geran drone
items.summary:
A laser air defense system developed by Ukrainian company Carmine Sky has reportedly shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran drone, according to Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, a radio technology specialist and adviser to Ukraine’s president. 

In a Telegram post on November 25, 2026, Beskrestnov said the Blysk laser, deployed to protect a critical infrastructure facility, had become the first combat laser in the world to shoot down a jet-powered Geran. 

Geran is Russia’s designation for its Shahed-type one-way attack drones. Beskrestnov shared a 21-second video of the interception but did not disclose when or where it took place or at what range. 

Ukraine deploys experimental lasers to protect infrastructure  

The Blysk laser is being developed under Ukraine’s state-backed Private Air Defense program, with support from the Brave1 defense technology cluster. 

Carmine Sky has already recorded successes under the program. On March 30, 2026, Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said the company had shot down Shahed and Zala drones over the Kharkiv region using its Sky Sentinel gun turret. 

According to Beskrestnov, several Ukrainian companies are now working on laser air defense systems, although the technology remains complex and expensive. 

“For now, it is too early to talk about serial production of the laser,” he wrote. However, the systems are already protecting critical infrastructure facilities as testing continues. 

Why jet-powered drones are harder to intercept  

Laser weapons have already been used successfully in combat. On May 28, 2025, Israel’s Ministry…
items.t: Ukrainian combat laser shoots down Russian jet-powered Geran drone

items.title: Ukraine says strike on major Russian air base damaged five military jets
items.summary:
Ukraine said it damaged three MiG-31 fighters and two Su-34 fighter-bombers in a strike on Russia’s Savasleyka air base, which Russian aircraft use to launch Kinzhal missiles at Ukraine.

Ukraine’s General Staff said the attack took place during a series of strikes on November 24 and overnight into November 25, 2026. Its preliminary assessment was that all five aircraft would be unable to fly for some time.

The military said it was still assessing the extent of the damage and the number of jets affected. Russia did not immediately comment.

Savasleyka is in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region, east of Moscow. Ukraine’s military said Russia uses the base to launch MiG-31s carrying Kinzhal air-launched ballistic missiles, which it has fired at Ukrainian cities.

The General Staff also reported strikes on a radar station and several fuel and supply depots in Russian-occupied parts of eastern Ukraine during the same operation.

The attack follows a Ukrainian strike in October 2026 on Seshcha airfield in Russia’s Bryansk region. That base is home to a Russian military transport regiment that operates Antonov An-124 cargo aircraft. Ukraine said at the time it was still assessing the damage there.

The post Ukraine says strike on major Russian air base damaged five military jets appeared first on AeroTime .
items.t: Ukraine says strike on major Russian air base damaged five military jets

items.title: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites for orbital data centers
items.summary:
The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) granted SpaceX conditional approval on November 25, 2026, to deploy up to 1 million satellites that would process data in orbit for use on Earth.

The constellation, called Starmind, is the first orbital data center network authorized by the FCC.

SpaceX applied in January 2026 for permission to launch and operate the network, which is intended to meet growing demand for artificial intelligence computing. The satellites would exchange data using laser links, with radio links available as a backup and for tracking and control.

The license gives SpaceX until November 2033 to put its first Starmind satellite into operation. It must have 100,000 in service by November 2035 and 500,000 by November 2038. The deadline for deploying the full constellation is November 2040.

SpaceX sought permission to move some satellites into other orbits at the end of their service lives. The FCC denied the waiver, saying SpaceX had provided too little information to show that its proposed disposal methods met the agency’s rules.

SpaceX would need a waiver before deploying Starmind satellites that it intends to retire without bringing them back through Earth’s atmosphere.

The American Astronomical Society and the Secure World Foundation were among the groups that raised concerns during the review. Their objections included the risk of collisions, interference with astronomical observations and the potential effects on the atmosphere as satellites burn up on reentry.

The FCC declined to conduct a comprehensive environmental review of the…
items.t: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites for orbital data centers

items.title: US proposes 10% tariff on Brazilian aircraft, putting Embraer sales at risk
items.summary:
The United States proposed a 10% tariff on finished aircraft imported from Brazil, putting Embraer at risk of higher costs in a market where US airlines have placed some of its largest regional jet orders.

The Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) wants to end an exemption for finished aircraft that it granted in July 2026, when Washington imposed a 25% tariff on certain Brazilian goods.

The new proposal, announced on November 25, 2026, would apply a 10% duty to several categories of finished aircraft, including airplanes and helicopters. The USTR said finished aircraft are Brazil’s fourth-largest export to the United States.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the proposed aircraft duty and separate measures on sugar were intended to increase pressure on Brazil in trade talks. The US wants talks covering a range of Brazilian policies, including digital payments, preferential tariffs, intellectual property and ethanol market access. Greer said Washington remained open to negotiations.

Embraer told Reuters it was reviewing the proposal and supported keeping aerospace trade tariff-free. The planemaker’s shares fell about 5% after the announcement.

American Airlines placed a firm order for 90 Embraer E175s in 2024, with purchase rights for 43 more. SkyWest ordered another 60 E175s in 2025, with purchase rights for 50 more aircraft and deliveries scheduled to begin in 2027.

Embraer’s business jet division has already felt the cost of US duties. In its latest earnings filing, the company said its executive aviation unit incurred $15 million in US import…
items.t: US proposes 10% tariff on Brazilian aircraft, putting Embraer sales at risk

items.title: Embraer opens new export route for KC-390 and A-29 through Brazil
items.summary:
Embraer has signed an agreement with Brazil’s state-owned aerospace company ALADA to facilitate sales of its KC-390 Millennium and A-29 Super Tucano through government-to-government (G2G) contracts. 

The two companies signed the framework agreement on November 25, 2026, at Mostra BID, Brazil’s national defense and security exhibition in Brasília. 

Embraer said the partnership would focus on undisclosed potential customers in Latin America and Africa. 

Brazil develops government-to-government export channel  

The agreement follows a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed at the FIDAE air show in Santiago, Chile, on April 7, 2026, when the two companies began exploring G2G sales opportunities. 

ALADA, formally Empresa de Projetos Aeroespaciais do Brasil, has been tasked by Brazil’s Ministry of Defense with facilitating government-to-government sales for the country’s defense industry. 

A memorandum between the ministry and ALADA, signed in March 2026, outlines how the process works. When a foreign government expresses interest in Brazilian defense equipment, the ministry can appoint ALADA to handle the transaction, sign export contracts and help the buyer select a Brazilian supplier. 

“This agreement establishes the conditions for countries that use the government-to-government procurement model to explore future opportunities to access Embraer’s portfolio,” said Fabio Caparica, Vice President of Contracts at Embraer Defense & Security. 

Sergio Roberto de Almeida, President of ALADA, called the agreement “a significant milestone for consolidating the G2G model in…
items.t: Embraer opens new export route for KC-390 and A-29 through Brazil

items.title: Thailand seeks to buy eight remaining Gripen E/F fighters in one order
items.summary:
The commander of the Royal Thai Air Force (RTAF), Air Chief Marshal Sakesan Kantha, has briefed Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on plans to buy eight more Saab Gripen E/F fighters in a single order instead of splitting the purchase into two batches. 

Speaking to reporters after a press conference marking the RTAF’s 90th anniversary in Bangkok on November 25, 2026, Sakesan said the relevant committees would submit detailed budget plans to the government, Thai newspaper Matichon reported . 

The proposal would combine the second and third phases of the procurement program, bringing the RTAF’s Gripen E/F fleet to a full squadron of 12 aircraft, including the four already on order. Sakesan said buying the remaining eight jets together would help avoid a capability gap and simplify negotiations over industrial offsets. 

Sakesan estimated the cost of the entire 12-aircraft program at around 60 billion baht ($1.77 billion). Preparations are set to begin in 2027, with funding to be sought in fiscal year 2028, the same year the aircraft the Gripens are replacing are due to retire. 

The proposal includes 10 offset measures, which Sakesan said he expected to bring economic benefits to Thailand worth more than the cost of the program itself. He did not elaborate on what those measures would involve. 

The air force chief had already outlined plans in July 2026 to seek funding for all eight remaining fighters at once.

items.t: Thailand seeks to buy eight remaining Gripen E/F fighters in one order
